901.author: yuanzhou75
901.body:
Fixes #900.

When an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint returns a 400 that explicitly rejects thinking/reasoning controls, retry the pre-stream request once with only those controls removed. Other 400 responses, and requests that have begun streaming, still fail normally.

Tests: added a model-client regression test for the one-shot fallback.

902.author: yuanzhou75
902.body:
Fixes #899.

The adapter now reports non-approval `chat.ask_user_question` frames as an external user-input wait. The JiuwenSwarm gateway pauses its run deadlines for that wait and resumes them on the next gateway event, so an unanswered clarification is no longer misclassified as idle progress failure.

Tests: `uv run --extra test pytest tests/test_events.py -q` (59 passed).

902.title: fix(adapter): pause deadlines for ask-user waits

904.author: moShangLouTou
904.body:
Desktop's built-in source switches currently change connector permissions, while Web source selection changes the sources sessions use by default. This can make a source appear enabled in Desktop without selecting its tools for an ordinary session. This PR makes the Desktop system settings page edit the global default source selection through `enabledConnectorIds`.

## Data source selection

- Rename the page to **Data sources** and add **Use by default** checkboxes for built-in and custom sources.
- Save the global `enabledConnectorIds` list while preserving unrelated overrides, instead of writing `plugins["connector.<id>"].enabled` for built-in selections. Retain the existing `web`-only fallback when the effective list is absent.
- Replace bulk enable/disable actions with **Select all / Clear selection** for listed sources. These actions change selection without reconnecting or disabling custom services.
- Keep custom MCP connection configuration separate: **Enable service** remains in the edit modal, alongside the existing edit, test and delete actions.
- Display catalog/service readiness independently of selection. Selecting a source does not establish that its service is ready or that its tools can be called.
- Update English/Chinese text and settings-page rendering tests.

This is a global defaults editor. It does not introduce a Desktop per-session selector or change backend selection, inheritance, permissions, or tool execution contracts. No settings migration is included.

## Validation

Tested commit: `7ed2300ff3735a71168d143815e6814790f6986f`.
Environment: Linux x86_64 / WSL2, Node.js v22.19.0; local shell executor, direct component/unit tests.

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`: **684 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`: **PASS**.
- `git diff --check`: **PASS**.
- The commit's code tree matches the original data-source commit exactly. The data-source and failure-notice changes were split without changing their combined code tree.

The settings tests exercise rendering; they do not prove persistence, cross-client reloads or effective session tool availability. Full local CI layers were not rerun as part of this branch split. Remote checks must be evaluated on this new head.

## Product journey coverage

**Not verified in this update:** Desktop/Web sharing a backend; selecting and clearing sources followed by a new inheriting session; explicit project/session overrides; specialist supplementation; disabled/unavailable custom services; native Windows/macOS Desktop. These remain acceptance evidence gaps for #852. Unit/component tests are not substitutes for these journeys.

Related: #852, #718.
The run-failure presentation changes are submitted separately and are no longer part of this PR.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix`. Applying the GitHub label is pending a maintainer because the contributor account lacks upstream label permissions.
User impact: Desktop source selection edits the session defaults rather than routine built-in permission switches.
Compatibility and migration: no schema changes; no migration included.
904.head: fix/desktop-mcp-data-source-selection
904.title: fix(desktop): align data source settings with global session defaults

905.author: moShangLouTou
905.body:
Desktop run failures expose raw provider diagnostics in the main conversation, including English error tokens in the Chinese UI. This PR presents localized recovery guidance first and keeps the original diagnostic information available under an expandable **Technical details** section.

## Failure presentation

- Map all seven `RunFailureCode` values to English/Chinese summaries: timeout, unauthorized, rate-limited, transport-error, server-error, invalid-tool-call and semantic-error.
- Use a generic fallback for missing or unrecognized codes. Resolve the active language when rendering.
- Keep the original error code and message in the expandable details block rather than replacing or discarding diagnostic information.
- Use neutral wording for `semantic-error`, since the backend uses it as a catch-all classification and it does not establish that a model service rejected the request.
- Apply the same localized summary and folded raw-message presentation to persisted `timeout_notice` messages.
- Add coverage for language switching, fallback codes, replayed failures, diagnostic preservation and a failed tool inside a successful run.

## Scope and remaining limitation

A timeout notice and a run-failed status can still both appear. The client cannot reliably associate a `timeout_notice` message with a specific run, so this PR keeps both visible. Reliable deduplication remains a follow-up requiring a suitable association contract. This partially addresses #846; it does not complete that issue's duplicate-alert criterion.

No backend error classifications, message schemas, toast behavior or data-source settings are changed. The data-source settings fix remains in #904. Both branches are independent and target `main`.

## Validation

Tested commit: `1de91124d4c1759f43952128a39cadebfda8efee`.
Environment: Linux x86_64 / WSL2, Node.js v22.19.0; local shell executor, direct component/unit tests using the existing dependency installation.

From `apps/desktop`:

- `tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx`: **700 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`: **PASS**.
- `git diff --check`: **PASS**.

The binaries above came from the existing Desktop dependency installation. The initial pnpm script invocations in the new worktree were blocked by pnpm's dependency-reinstallation/no-TTY check; the equivalent underlying scripts then passed without reinstalling dependencies. The two split branches recombine to precisely the original PR code tree. Full local CI layers were not rerun for this split, and remote checks must be assessed on the new head.

## Product journey coverage

**Not verified in this update:** producing a real run failure through a supported Desktop entry point, expanding diagnostics in the running UI, persisted-session reloads against a live backend, and native Windows/macOS Desktop. The tests cover component rendering and formatting; they do not establish these end-to-end outcomes. Product journey evidence and required checks remain outstanding.

Related: #846, #718.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix`. Applying the GitHub label is pending a maintainer because the contributor account lacks upstream label permissions.
User impact: localized failure guidance with diagnostics available on demand.
Compatibility and migration: no schema changes or migration.


## CodeCheck follow-up validation

Commit: `922122f9d09e924e6a184a4759b9f5ab1968f858`. Removed the redundant `as string` assertion in `apps/desktop/src/run-failure.ts`; the indexed message expression is already typed as `string`. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

On this commit, Linux x86_64 / WSL2, Node.js v22.19.0, local shell executor with the existing dependency installation:

- From `apps/desktop`, `tsx --test tests/run-failure.test.ts tests/assistant-turn.test.tsx tests/conversation.test.tsx`: **60 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`: **PASS**.
- `git diff --check`: **PASS**.

These targeted results are separate from the earlier 700-test result above. Full CI and product journeys were not rerun for this type-only cleanup. A new CodeCheck result is still required; local tests and typechecking do not establish that the remote scan passed.
905.head: fix/desktop-run-failure-notices
905.title: fix(desktop): localize run-failure notices and fold raw diagnostics

906.author: qingkwl
906.body:
First batch of the first-message latency plan (#799): warm the MCP catalog while the user is still on the ready screen, and stop paying a second `skills.list` RPC on every run that imports nothing. Together they address the two largest measured chunks of the first message — the ~48s stdio catalog cold-start (field) and part of the ~4s `skills.list` x3 chain in the SD-side run preparation.

## Warm the MCP catalog right after agent-ready (S1)

On a fresh install the bundled stdio MCP servers spawn and enumerate their tools on the first chat run; field measurements put this chunk at ~48s of the 60-135s first-message latency. The shell's `watchAgentReady` already polls `/agent/info`, and the moment `jiuwenswarm.reachable` turns true it now issues `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload` in the background — the MCP settings page's refresh request, and the one endpoint that actually connects and enumerates. The spawns and tool enumeration then overlap the ready screen instead of the first message.

The endpoint choice was corrected during live verification (commit ef65229e): the first revision fired `GET /api/mcp/sources`, which only reads the cached manifest/status list — on a running stack it answered 200 in ~1s and spawned nothing, and the first chat run still paid the full catalog load. The reload endpoint spawned every bundled source in ~3.3s on the same stack, with the stdio processes visible on the host. Verified locally: catalog warmed at boot → a first message afterwards pays zero MCP chunk (E1.6 evidence pack).

Best-effort by contract: failures are logged to `shell.log` (`[warmup] first-chat /api/mcp/sources/reload -> <status>` or a failure line) and never surface to the user. When the warmup loses the race, the run path re-runs the same steps — no behavioural fork, only a head start.

## One `skills.list` per sync when nothing imports (S3a)

`SkillSync.sync()` ran `skills.list` twice per run: `_sync()` listed to diff staged skills against JiuwenSwarm's, and the tail listed again to refresh the adapter's `directories` map. That map only carries ScienceDiscovery-marked skills, which can only appear through this adapter's own imports — a run that imports nothing changes no directory, so the second listing was the first one's answer. `_sync()` now reports whether it imported anything; `sync()` re-lists only then. The import path is byte-for-byte today's behaviour (pre-import listing + post-import refresh); the steady-state path saves one RPC round trip per run and still populates the map from the single listing, including right after an adapter restart.

This is step S3a of the run-preparation-chain plan; S3c (acceptance-path parallelisation) remains a follow-up.

## One `skills.list` per run, cached 30s with write-through invalidation (S3b)

After S3a a steady-state run still paid two `skills.list` RPCs: `_sync()` listed to diff staged skills, and the API's reconcile listed again through `GET /agent/skills`. Both read the same list, and the adapter performs every write to that list itself (`skills.import_local` in `_import`, `skills.toggle` in `set_enabled`) — so a short-TTL cache with write-through invalidation serves both reads from one fetch while keeping the cached answer at least as fresh as the last write. Back-to-back runs staging the same skills now send **one `skills.list` per run instead of two**; an import or a toggle invalidates immediately, and a zero TTL restores today's fetch-every-read behaviour as the kill switch.

A cache hit never changes what JiuwenSwarm receives: import decisions still run against the freshest answer the adapter itself has written, and a direct JW-side edit can only stay invisible for the 30s TTL — the trade the plan documents. Step S3b of the run-preparation plan.

## Validation

- `pnpm --dir win_desktop build` — clean (esbuild).
- `pnpm --dir win_desktop typecheck` — clean (tsc).
- `pnpm --dir win_desktop test` — 164 pass / 0 fail (5 first-chat-warmup tests: URL/header construction, POST method to the reload endpoint, happy path, failure propagation, timeout bounds; baseline was 159 before this change).
- Live stack check (dev stack, 2026-11-05): `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload` with the shell's auth header returned 200 in ~3.3s and spawned all 13 bundled stdio sources (`ready`); the prior `GET` on the same stack returned 200 in ~1s and spawned nothing — this is what motivated the endpoint fix.
- Adapter: `uv run pytest tests/` (services/adapter) — 292 passed, 1 failed. The failure, `test_diagnostics.py::test_private_rotating_file`, is pre-existing on this host: it fails identically on the unmodified base commit in the same worktree (verified with `git stash`), and the change does not touch diagnostics. All 15 skills tests pass, including 5 that count the RPCs: a no-import sync lists exactly once and still populates the directories map (S3a); an importing sync still lists twice (pre-import + post-import refresh, S3a unchanged); two `listed()` calls within the TTL share one RPC, a no-import sync and the next `listed()` share one RPC (S3b); an import and a toggle each invalidate so the next read re-fetches (S3b); a zero TTL restores fetch-every-read (S3b kill switch).
- Not covered here: packaged-install validation (GUI-interactive install, three boot profiles, cold-install first message). That needs an installer build and a quiet machine; it is scheduled and will be reported before this PR is marked ready.

## E2E user journeys

Local stack (dev tree, base 79d26dd6 + this branch), mock OpenAI endpoint on loopback answering SSE in ~30 ms, quiet load window, same-window pairs (D5 discipline: fresh session first message vs same-session second, median of 3):

1. **Warmup fires end-to-end (the S1 claim).** Desktop shell launched against the live stack; `shell.log` recorded `[warmup] first-chat /api/mcp/sources/reload -> 200`, and the API log recorded `mcp_catalog_loaded durationMs=3846 failedServerCount=0 serverCount=3 toolCount=39` in the same second. The 6 bundled stdio MCP server processes were visible on the host before any message was sent. PASS.
2. **First/second message, web-only connectors (E1 anatomy口径).** First message 5.5s / 9.4s / (one round lost to a transient Windows file-lock EPERM, retried clean) — median ≈ 5.5-9.4s; second message 3.5s median. The 2026-11-03 baseline on the old base was 26.09s / 8.67s; the drop is mostly upstream work landed in the meantime (patch 0020 moved the 12.4s observability import off the hot-start path) plus the quiet load window — this pair is reported as no-regression evidence, not as S1/S3a attribution. PASS (no regression).
3. **First message with an MCP tool call, cold vs warm catalog (the S1 mechanism).** Session with `enabledConnectorIds: ["web","uniprot"]`, mock model answers the prompt with one `mcp__uniprot__search` call. Cold catalog (API boot refresh had failed: `mcp_connection_failed … MCP connection timeout` × 3 servers at startup, as it does on this host): run completed in ~7.7s with the catalog load inside the run. Warm catalog (after `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload`, the exact S1 request): run completed in 5.7s, tool call answered in 16ms, no connection events in the run window. Delta ≈ 2s on this warm-filesystem dev box; the field cold-install figure the plan cites is ~48s (E1.6 evidence). PASS — the warmup demonstrably moves the catalog load out of the first run.
4. **S3a mechanism.** Adapter unit tests count the RPCs directly (a no-import sync sends exactly one `skills.list`, an importing sync still sends two); the dev-stack venv still runs the pre-S3a adapter build, so the in-stack numbers above are the conservative (two-list) path. PASS by unit test; in-stack A/B lands when the venv is refreshed.

Failure attribution: the only run failures in the session were transient host file-lock EPERMs on skill-snapshot rename (Windows antivirus/indexer) — retried clean, not product failures. The pre-existing `test_private_rotating_file` failure is documented in Validation above.

Commands: `node .tmp/mock-openai.mjs` (mock, SSE instant), `node .tmp/fml-ab.mjs 3` and `node .tmp/fml-s1-ab.mjs cold|warm` (drivers; client-side SSE timing + event timeline). Counts: journey 1 = 1/1 PASS; journey 2 = 5/6 runs clean (1 env-retry); journey 3 = 1/1 cold + 1/1 warm PASS; journey 4 = 10/10 unit tests.

## Release

Release category: `release:performance` (GitHub label pending a maintainer — the author has read-only access to the upstream repository and cannot apply it).
User impact: faster first message on installed builds (the MCP catalog no longer cold-starts inside the first chat run) and slightly cheaper every run (one fewer `skills.list` round trip in the steady state). No UI change, no configuration change, no behaviour change on failure paths.
Compatibility and migration: none.
906.head: first-message-latency
906.title: perf(win_desktop,adapter): first-message latency - MCP catalog warmup at agent-ready, one skills.list per sync

907.body: A report could only describe what broke in words, so triage often needed a round-trip to ask for the screen the user was looking at. Both shells can now attach up to eight screenshots, the Worker publishes them into the feedback repository and embeds them in the issue, and the submission client lives in `operational-logging` so the web and desktop copies cannot drift. The dialog is reshaped around the description: the screenshot picker sits directly under it, the panel is wider and shorter, and frequency/impact are asked only for a problem report. On the web the two entry points are merged into one 我要反馈 action, with the GitHub route kept as a prominent link in the dialog's top-right corner, and the web controls now follow the desktop scale so both shells read as one product. /kind feature **What this PR does / why we need it**: - `packages/operational-logging`: shared `FeedbackImage` contract (max 8 images, 2 MiB each, decoded-size validation), image preparation and `submitFeedback` client, and sanitisation of image names in the payload. - `packages/feedback-worker`: accepts `images`, uploads them through the GitHub contents API, embeds them in the issue body, and keeps the report when one upload fails; dedupe covers the image set. `wrangler.toml` keeps dashboard variables (`keep_vars = true`) and the README documents the configuration. - `apps/web` / `apps/desktop`: screenshot picker under the description, thumbnails and removal, image errors, wider/shorter dialog, triage grid rendered only for problems, and a single 我要反馈 entry on web instead of the duplicate GitHub button (the link now lives in the dialog). - Shared client extraction (`feedback-client.ts`) with thin per-shell adapters; i18n and `feedback.css` updates on both sides. **Which issue(s) this PR fixes**: Follow-up to #843. **What scenarios were tested, and what were the verification results（Function, performance, reliability, etc.）**： - `pnpm typecheck` clean. - `feedback-worker` 17/17: CORS, request/image size limits, dedupe with a changed screenshot, daily quota, 422 label fallback, screenshot upload, and a failed upload still creating the issue. - `operational-logging` 15/15: image count/MIME/Base64/decoded-size validation and payload sanitisation. - Web feedback suites 19/19, desktop feedback suites 18/18. - Manual on `localhost:5173` and `127.0.0.1:5174`: switched 遇到问题 / 有想法 / 其他 to confirm frequency and impact appear only for problems, added and removed screenshots, and opened the GitHub link from the dialog's top-right corner. **Self-checklist**: - [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes. - [x] Added/updated tests for the new behaviour (image validation, upload, dedupe, triage visibility). - [x] Updated the README and configuration docs. - [x] No secrets or personal data are added; diagnostics are redacted before they leave the client. ## Visual evidence Captured locally on `b5783b4f` with Edge at 1440×900 (2× DPR), in both `zh` and `en`. The files are committed under `docs/images/feedback/` on the evidence branch [`docs/pr907-feedback-screenshots`](https://github.com/nanzhaogang/sciencediscovery/tree/docs/pr907-feedback-screenshots/docs/images/feedback), so these links stay stable. ### Dialog after the reshape (default: 遇到问题 / Report a problem) | Web (zh) | Web (en) | | --- | --- | | | | | Desktop (zh) | Desktop (en) | | --- | --- | | | | ### Picker with several thumbnails attached (one capture per shell) | Web (zh) | Web (en) | | --- | --- | | | | | Desktop (zh) | Desktop (en) | | --- | --- | | | | ### Removing an attached image | Web (zh) | Web (en) | | --- | --- | | | | | Desktop (zh) | Desktop (en) | | --- | --- | | | | ### Unsupported file type: the inline error is per image and the report stays intact | Web (zh) | Web (en) | | --- | --- | | | | | Desktop (zh) | Desktop (en) | | --- | --- | | | | ### 有想法 / 其他: 出现频率 and 影响程度 are gone Web, 有想法: Desktop: | 有想法 (zh) | 其他 (zh) | | --- | --- | | | | | Suggest an idea (en) | Other (en) | | --- | --- | | | | ### Web entry point: "我要反馈" opens the dialog, the GitHub option is in the dialog header | zh | en | | --- | --- | | | |

908.author: HugoXK
908.body:
Fixes #884

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What is wrong

`GET /api/sessions/:session/artifact-versions/:version/diff` answered **500 `Internal server error`** when either version of the pair is not textual, and logged a false `unclassified_request_error`. `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:357` threw a plain `Error("Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions")`, whose prose matches no client-input pattern in `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` and no not-found mapper in `services/api/src/http/index.ts`, so the top-level catch classified a client-input problem as a server fault.

Measured at `7057aaf6` with two `application/zip` versions of one artifact in one session (red commit `0be111de` only):

```
GET /api/sessions/<id>/artifact-versions/<version>/diff
500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
```

The same request, with logging configured the way `startPlatform` does (not by `createApiServer` alone), wrote:

```
ERROR [api] event=unclassified_request_error errorMessage="Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions" method=GET path=/api/sessions/<id>/artifact-versions/<version>/diff status=500
```

## The fix — option 2 from the issue, in the helper

`artifactVersionDiff` now throws `new ApiStatusError(400, "Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions")`. The rejection is classified by **class** (the top-level catch answers `ApiStatusError.statusCode` before any prose matching), and it sits where the rule lives, so every caller of the helper answers the same 400 instead of only this route. No new message pattern was added to `isKnownClientInputError`.

The versions both exist; this is not a missing resource, which is why it is a 400 and not the 404 family `#881` adds.

### Why the route was not touched (overlap with #881)

`#881` (ours, open) rewrites the `diff` route block in `services/api/src/http/index.ts` for the missing-`to` / missing-`against` cases. Hoisting the media-type check into that same block would (a) collide textually with `#881`, and (b) put the from-version resolution in two places: the route would have to repeat what the helper already computes, and the next caller of the helper would get the 500 again. This fix touches only `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts`; the two behaviours are complementary (`#881` = missing version, this = both present but not comparable), so whichever lands second keeps both without a conflict.

### Import note

`services/api/src/runs/index.ts` already imports `artifacts/index.ts`, so importing `ApiStatusError` from `runs` inside `artifacts` would have closed a cycle between two large modules. The class therefore lives in `services/api/src/http/api-status-error.ts`, which imports nothing; `runs/index.ts` imports it and re-exports it (its public API is unchanged, so the existing import in `services/api/src/http/index.ts` still works), and `artifacts/index.ts` imports the leaf directly. No reverse edge was added and no cycle exists.

The leaf move keeps the identity check honest: `services/api/src/http/index.ts` still matches `error instanceof ApiStatusError` against the class the helper throws, which the new test proves by driving that exact path — a divergent class object would answer 500, not the 400 asserted there.

## Red → green

`services/api/src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts` (test-only commit `0be111de`) seeds versions through `SessionStore.createArtifactVersion` and asks the real route, so no execution is driven: an `application/zip` pair, a pair that switches from `text/markdown` to `application/zip`, and a `text/markdown` control pair that must keep diffing.

Red at `7057aaf6`:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts
not ok 1 - a non-textual artifact pair answers a client error instead of 500
  error: |-
    binary pair must answer 400 with the reason, not 500
      body: { error: 'Internal server error' }
      status: 500
# tests 1 / # pass 0 / # fail 1
```

Green at `207243a7` (same command): `1 test / 1 pass / 0 fail`, exit 0. That run was still green by luck — see the review fix below.

The false log is gone in the same manual repro: `STATUS 400 {"error":"Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions"}`, `grep -c unclassified_request_error` → `0`, and the request is logged as `http_request_failed … statusCode=400`.

## Review fix — the fixture seeded after the server's `ready` chain

`sciencediscovery-bot`'s thread on `artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts:130` is right and this is a test-only correction: `createApiServer` returns before `ready` (which ends in `store.load()`) has run, and the fixture seeded after `server.listen`, so the test passed only when the seeds landed before that load. Two commits, no product code changed:

- `b3eb58b8` makes the ordering explicit: a request settles `ready` before the seeds. It is red, deterministically, on a machine that starts the server quickly:
  ```
  not ok 1 - a non-textual artifact pair answers a client error instead of 500
      binary pair must answer 400 with the reason, not 500
      +     error: 'Internal server error'
      +   status: 500
  ```
  (the 500 is the pre-fix behaviour: the route's `store` has already loaded a catalog without these versions, `getArtifactVersion` returns `undefined`, and `artifacts/index.ts` throws the plain `Error("Artifact version not found")`.)
- `76e911b5` removes the race instead of winning it: `startHttpFixture` is split into `createFixture` + `startHttpServer(context, fixture)`, the test writes every version first and starts the server afterwards, so `ready` loads a catalog that already contains them. No wait, retry or timeout is involved.

Green five consecutive runs of the same command, one process each:

```
[run 1] # pass 1 # fail 0
[run 2] # pass 1 # fail 0
[run 3] # pass 1 # fail 0
[run 4] # pass 1 # fail 0
[run 5] # pass 1 # fail 0
```

`tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` exit 0; `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` exit 0. This review fix alone is `1 file, +14/−7` (`git diff --stat 207243a7..76e911b5`).

## Validation

| gate | command | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| new test, red | `node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts` | `1/0/1`, exit 1 (at `7057aaf6` + test commit) |
| new test, green | same | `1 test / 1 pass / 0 fail`, exit 0 (at `207243a7`) |
| UT slice for the touched module | `node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts src/artifact-lifecycle.test.ts src/provenance.test.ts src/dashboard.test.ts` | `88 tests / 88 pass / 0 fail`, exit 0 (at `207243a7`) |
| typecheck (api) | `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` | exit 0, 0 errors |
| typecheck (tests project) | `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` | exit 0, 0 errors |

Environment note, so the numbers are reproducible: this worktree's `node_modules` predates the current lockfile and the sandbox cannot write to the pnpm store, so `@types/ssh2` (declared by `packages/executor`) and the `packages/feedback-worker/node_modules` workspace link were missing before the first typecheck run. Without them the api typecheck reported 18 errors, all in `packages/executor/src/ssh-connection.ts` / `ssh-keys.ts` (missing `ssh2` declarations) and the tests typecheck 4 in `packages/feedback-worker` — none in the touched files. Installing the declared `@types/ssh2` into the local `node_modules` and adding that workspace link brings both to exit 0; no repository file was changed for it.

Not run: the full `services/api` UT suite (only the module slice above), the L2/ST/E2E layers, and a real server with a real artifact-producing execution — the route test seeds the catalog directly because the media-type rule is checked before any CAS read, which is exactly the point the issue makes.

`git diff --stat 7057aaf6…HEAD`: 4 files, `+247/−13` (`artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts` +199, `http/api-status-error.ts` +34, `runs/index.ts` +6/−12, `artifacts/index.ts` +8/−1), 5 commits (`0be111de` test, `b6de0d8e` fix, `207243a7` the class move that removes the import cycle, `b3eb58b8` red and `76e911b5` green for the review fix above).

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: comparing two binary artifact versions (two `.zip` uploads, a text version against a later binary one) now answers `400 {"error":"Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions"}` instead of `500 Internal server error`, and the server no longer logs a false `unclassified_request_error` for a request the client can avoid. Textual pairs still diff as before.

Compatibility and migration: none — the 400 body is the message the helper already carried; only its status and classification change.

913.author: ink999107
913.body:
`search_preprints` asked the provider for `/{days}d/0/json`. bioRxiv and medRxiv answer that request with HTTP 200, an empty `collection`, and a "Both dates must be in yyyy-mm-dd format" message, so the gateway read a rejected request as "no matches" and the assistant told users the window contained no preprints.

## Dated-range requests

`config/external-urls.json` now carries a `yyy-mm-dd` range template instead of the invalid `{days}d` form, and `_preprint_search` computes the window in UTC (`days=1` yields a single-day range). UTC avoids "today" landing in the provider's future.

## Provider failures are no longer silent

A `messages[0].status` that reports a rejected request now raises instead of returning a clean empty result. Invalid requests still return HTTP 200, so this status message is the only failure signal the provider gives.

An empty window is not a rejection: the provider answers one with its own status, `no posts found`, and no `total`. That status is accepted and mapped onto the existing empty-window warning — "The provider reports no preprints published between …" — so a `days=1` search on a quiet day, or a category with nothing in the window, returns an empty result rather than a tool error.

## Newest-first scanning within the tool deadline

The provider serves a window oldest-first, and its trailing path segment is a record offset, not a page number: measured on both servers, cursor 1 starts one record after cursor 0, so adjacent cursors share 29 of 30 records. The search starts at the newest offset and walks backwards, dedupes DOIs that shift between pages while the window moves, and reports how much of the window it actually scanned. Previously the warning implied the whole window had been filtered.

The walk has to fit the 30 s deadline that the Node MCP transport gives a search tool call, so it spends a wall-clock budget rather than counting pages:

- one HTTP client for the whole scan, so pages reuse the connection instead of paying a TLS handshake each;
- the newest page alone first, because it usually fills `limit`, then up to four pages in flight;
- a 20 s stop, leaving headroom for the answer to return, with the warning saying the scan stopped early;
- each page gets the budget that is left, so a slow page costs that page and not the
  pages of its batch that already answered;
- one reconnect when the provider closes an idle keep-alive connection between pages.

The page fetched to learn `total` (offset 0) is reused as the tail of the walk instead of being downloaded and discarded; coverage counts distinct offsets, so the reused tail is not reported twice.

## Validation

- Gateway suite: 42 tests, 42 passed, 0 failed.
  `PYTHONPATH=services/gateway/src python -m unittest discover -s services/gateway/tests -p 'test_*.py'`
  (run from the branch head with the service virtualenv because workspace dependency preparation could not complete in this environment — see below).
- L1 slice on this head: planned 4, executed 4, passed 4, failed 0, skipped 0.
- Live provider smoke, no mocks:
  - Empty window: bioRxiv `liver`, 1 day, `category=zoology` → 0 records, warning "The provider reports no preprints published between 2026-11-05 to 2026-11-05", answered in 2.5 s. Before this round the same call raised.
  - medRxiv `diabetes`, 30 days, limit 3 → 2 records from the newest page, "Scanned 30 of 1873 … stopped at its 20-second time budget". The host used for this smoke fetched 6–9 s per page at the time, so the budget, not the scan design, ended it.
  - bioRxiv `liver`, 30 days, limit 5 → "Scanned 30 of 7257", stopped at the time budget, 0 records from that page; the same query returned 5 records when the host's per-page latency was under 2 s.
  - `lookup_doi` for a returned bioRxiv DOI: still returns its versions (no regression).
- Not run locally: UT, ST and E2E. The shared runner's preparation (`uv sync`) stalls downloading dependency wheels from the PyPI CDN at roughly 20 KB/s in this environment; switching to a mirror conflicts with the committed lockfile. No assertion was weakened or skipped to work around it. The gateway suite above exercises the changed code, and CI runs the full layers on this head.

## E2E user journeys

BLOCKED: the mocked browser E2E layer was not run for the reason above. The affected path is an MCP tool invoked by the assistant rather than a browser journey; the live provider smoke in Validation is the substitute evidence for it. Tested SHA: b87fa499.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: bioRxiv and medRxiv searches return matching recent preprints instead of an always-empty list; a rejected provider request surfaces as an error rather than as "no results"; an empty date window stays an empty result. The tool warning now states how much of the date window was scanned and whether the scan stopped early.

Compatibility and migration: the configuration key `data_sources.preprints.details_by_days_template` is replaced by `data_sources.preprints.details_by_range_template`; a deployment that uses a customized copy of `config/external-urls.json` must apply the same rename. Running gateway processes must be restarted because the URL table is cached in-process.

Labels: `release:fix`, `bug` and `bot-reviewed` are applied.
913.head: fix/biorxiv-preprint-search
913.title: fix(gateway): return real bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint search results

915.author: HugoXK
915.body:
Fixes #914

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## Problem

`UT` on PR #890 (tip `fdb835fb`, run `42015883088`, job `127206585414`) failed `services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py::ArchitectureBoundaryTests::test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names` with a `FileNotFoundError` instead of an assertion:

```
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
'.../services/api/.tmp/agent-skill-creator-1793877061398-12103/projects/.../skill-snapshots/.716ffbc5-....skill-snapshot/antibody-design/scripts/install_pipeline_deps.sh'
```

The UT layer read `planned 6366 / executed 6366 / passed 6365 / failed 1 / skipped 0`; the group holding it was `1 failed, 30 passed in 4.55s` (the other 30 gateway Python tests ran normally). The same test set was green on the previous tip of that branch (`c4fb33d4`, run `41890794011`), and the failing PR's diff touches neither `services/gateway` nor `services/api/.tmp`.

## Cause

`_files()` walks `services/api`, `packages`, `apps/web` and `test/api` and skips only `__pycache__`, `dist`, `node_modules`. `services/api/.tmp` is a live runtime workspace root, not source: `services/api/src/server.test.ts` and the skill-creator paths create session trees there while other workers run and delete them after. The walk lists a path, the owning test removes it, `read_text()` raises, and the boundary assertion is replaced by an error that has nothing to do with the pull request's diff. The cost is a full CI cycle plus a rerun that we cannot trigger ourselves.

## Red first

Two deterministic regression tests at `7057aaf6` (test commit `1c7817a2`). Both create their probe under `services/api/.tmp` and remove it in cleanup:

```
FAILED services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py::GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests::test_a_workspace_file_removed_after_listing_is_skipped
E   FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../services/api/.tmp/probe-boundary-3.ts'

FAILED services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py::GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests::test_a_generated_workspace_is_not_walked
E   AssertionError: 'content: services/api/.tmp/probe-boundary-3.ts' unexpectedly found in ['content: services/api/.tmp/probe-boundary-3.ts']

2 failed, 3 passed, 1 warning in 7.71s
```

The first reproduces the CI shape exactly without relying on timing: the listing yields a path that is already gone when the walk reads it. The second is the `.tmp` root itself being walked as source. Both fail on `main` and pass after the fix.

## After fix

Two changes, one file:

- `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` gains `.tmp`: like `dist`, it is generated runtime data, not source.
- The read side treats `FileNotFoundError` as "the file vanished after the listing" and skips that path: a source file removed mid-walk cannot be asserted on, and an assertion is not what we want to raise here.

```
$ python3 -m pytest services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py -q
5 passed, 1 warning in 3.93s
```

`git diff --stat 7057aaf6..HEAD`: 1 file, `+69/−13` (`services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py`). `_node_boundary_failures()` is the walk extracted from the existing test so both the original assertion and the regression tests exercise the same code path.

Not run: the full `services/gateway/tests` suite and CI; this file is the gate for this issue.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: none for users; a CI layer no longer fails on unrelated pull requests when an API test deletes its temporary workspace while the architecture-boundary walk is reading it.
Compatibility and migration: none.
915.head: dev2/fix/914-architecture-boundary-tmp-race
915.title: fix(gateway): keep the architecture-boundary walk out of services/api/.tmp

921.author: HugoXK
921.body: Fixes #919 ## Problem PR #892 gives `cancelled` its own summary bucket in `apps/web/src/WakeNotice.tsx`, and `apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx` covers only that one case — a single `cancelled` record. Nothing pins the other side of the same rule: `queued`, `running`, `unknown` and a record with **no `state`** must keep falling through to `unconfirmed`, and a mixed notice must summarise one entry per bucket. A future bucket, or a reordering of the filter chain, can reclassify those states with the suite still green. ## Cause The outcome line is built from three filters over `notice.records`: ``` completed = records.filter(state === "completed") failed = records.filter(state === "failed") unconfirmed= records.filter(state !== "completed" && state !== "failed") ``` `RuntimeNoticeRecord.state` is optional (`packages/schema/src/session.ts:138`), so the catch-all is the only thing that keeps every state without a bucket of its own visible — and after #892 shifted that boundary, no test asserted the fall-through side or the per-bucket join. ## Change One file, tests only — no product code: `apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx`, **+36/−0** (1 file). 1. `a notice under way still summarises as unconfirmed, not as its own bucket` — `records` with `queued`, `running`, `unknown`, and one object with no `state` renders `4 unconfirmed` and no `cancelled` bucket. 2. `a mixed notice summarises each outcome bucket instead of collapsing them` — `1 completed + 1 failed + 1 cancelled` renders `1 completed · 1 failed · 1 cancelled` plus the three badges. ## Red-first evidence Command, from `apps/web`: `node --import tsx --test tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx` **Baseline (this branch on today's `main`, i.e. before #892 is merged)** — case 1 already holds, case 2 is red because the bucket it pins does not exist yet: ``` ok 3 - a notice under way still summarises as unconfirmed, not as its own bucket not ok 4 - a mixed notice summarises each outcome bucket instead of collapsing them # tests 5 # pass 4 # fail 1 ``` The failing assertion is exactly the missing bucket: ``` The input did not match the regular expression /1 completed · 1 failed · 1 cancelled/. Input: '… 1 completed · 1 failed · 1 unconfirmed …' ``` With #892's product change applied locally (`git checkout faeb95df -- apps/web/src/WakeNotice.tsx apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`, **not** committed, reverted afterwards): `# tests 5 / # pass 5 / # fail 0`. That is the tree this branch reaches as soon as #892 is on `main`. **Case 1's red-first demonstration** — temporarily adding `&& record.state !== "running"` to the catch-all (the regression the test exists to catch: a state silently losing the fall-through): ``` not ok 3 - a notice under way still summarises as unconfirmed, not as its own bucket The input did not match the regular expression /4 unconfirmed/. Input: '… 3 unconfirmed …' # tests 5 / # pass 3 / # fail 2 ``` Product file restored with `git checkout`, working tree clean again (`git status` shows only the test file). ## Dependency: #892 This PR is a **draft** on purpose. Case 2 pins the `cancelled` bucket that #892 introduces, so its UT job is green only once #892 is on `main`; drafts skip UT/ST (`ci.yml:26`), so no red check is created in the meantime. After #892 merges I rebase onto the new `main`, re-run the file, re-do the case-1 red-first demo on the final tree and report the new tip before this is marked ready. ## Reads Ran: - `node --import tsx --test tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx` (in `apps/web`) — baseline `5 tests / 4 pass / 1 fail`; against #892's tree `5 / 5 / 0`; catch-all broken `5 / 3 / 2`. - `../../node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` (in `apps/web`) — exit 0, no output. - `git diff --numstat upstream/main..HEAD` — `36 0 apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx`. Not run: - `pnpm ci:l1` locally — its prepare step runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, which cannot write the local pnpm store here; CI runs L1 on this PR (drafts run policy + L1). - UT/ST layers locally — draft PRs skip them until ready; the numbers above are the same file run directly with the same runner (`tsx --test`).

922.author: HugoXK
922.body:
Fixes #665

`web_fetch`'s public-URL guard still lets four IPv6 families through even though each one carries an IPv4 address the guard already knows how to judge. A model-supplied URL such as `http://[64:ff9b::7f00:1]/` or `http://[2002:a9fe:a9fe::]/` reaches loopback or the link-local metadata endpoint, while the equivalent `::ffff:127.0.0.1` is rejected. This closes those four holes and pins both directions — blocked literals stay blocked, public embedded addresses stay routable.

## What was wrong

`ipv6Blocked()` only consults `ipv4Blocked()` for IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) and IPv4-compatible (`::a.b.c.d`) forms, where the embedded IPv4 address sits in the last two hextets. Four other families carry the same address somewhere else:

| family | prefix | where the IPv4 address sits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NAT64 well-known | `64:ff9b::/96` | last 32 bits |
| NAT64 local-use | `64:ff9b:1::/48` | last 32 bits |
| 6to4 | `2002::/16` | hextets 2–3 |
| IPv4-translated | `::ffff:0:0:0/96` | last 32 bits, after `ffff` and 16 zero bits |
| Teredo | `2001:0::/32` | last 32 bits, bitwise inverted |
| site-local (deprecated) | `fec0::/10` | no IPv4 — the range itself is non-public |

No branch inspected those positions, so each form fell through to `return false`.

## What changed

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts` gains one helper, `dotted(high, low)`, and `ipv6Blocked()` learns to extract the embedded address for the six rows above and hand it to the existing `ipv4Blocked()` — the documented prefixes are matched, the address is decoded, and the verdict is the same predicate that already rejects `127.0.0.1` and `169.254.169.254`. There is no second copy of the IPv4 block list, no blanket range ban, and no refactor of the existing mapped/compatible branches: `ipv6Blocked()` keeps its shape and the new decoders delegate.

Teredo needs the inversion because the client address is stored XOR-ed with `0xffffffff`; `2001:0:808:808::80ff:fffe` therefore decodes to client `127.0.0.1`, not to the relay `128.255.255.254`.

The test computes nothing itself: it asserts the same 15 cases from both directions, plus the literal path (`assertPublicUrl("http://[...]/")`) and the resolver path (`assertPublicUrl(url, resolver)`), so a future change that fixes only literals fails.

## Red first

The new test, run against the unfixed `url-guard.ts` (`git checkout <test-commit> -- url-guard.ts`):

```
# Subtest: web_fetch judges NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local literals by their embedded IPv4
not ok 11 - web_fetch judges NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local literals by their embedded IPv4
  ---
  error: |-
    64:ff9b::7f00:1

    false !== true

  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
  name: 'AssertionError'
  expected: true
  actual: false
  operator: 'strictEqual'
# pass 15
# fail 1
```

The loop stops at the first failing literal, so the same nine blocked literals were also probed one by one against the unfixed predicate — each line below is one assertion that fails with `false !== true`:

```
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("64:ff9b::7f00:1"), true, "NAT64 /96 -> 127.0.0.1")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe"), true, "NAT64 /96 -> 169.254.169.254")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("64:ff9b:1::7f00:1"), true, "NAT64 /48 -> 127.0.0.1")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("2002:7f00:1::"), true, "6to4 -> 127.0.0.1")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("2002:a9fe:a9fe::"), true, "6to4 -> 169.254.169.254")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("::ffff:0:7f00:1"), true, "IPv4-translated -> 127.0.0.1")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("::ffff:0:a9fe:a9fe"), true, "IPv4-translated -> 169.254.169.254")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("fec0::1"), true, "site-local")  // false !== true
assert.equal(isBlockedAddress("2001:0:808:808::80ff:fffe"), true, "Teredo -> client 127.0.0.1")  // false !== true
```

## After the fix

```
# tests 16
# pass 16
# fail 0
```

The reverse direction is asserted in the same test, so the fix cannot be "block the prefix": `64:ff9b::808:808`, `64:ff9b:1::808:808`, `2002:808:808::`, `::ffff:0:808:808`, `2001:0:808:808::f7f7:f7f7` (Teredo for `8.8.8.8`) and `2606:4700:4700::1111` all stay routable, both as literals and through `assertPublicUrl`.

Diffstat against `main` `f4dd1813`:

```
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/providers.test.ts | 49 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts      | 29 +++++++++++--
 2 files changed, 75 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)
```

Ran:
- `node --import tsx --test src/web/native/providers.test.ts` in `packages/data-source` — `# tests 16 # pass 16 # fail 0`; the same command on the unfixed source is the red above (`# pass 15 # fail 1`).
- `tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- Per-literal probe of the nine blocked addresses against the unfixed predicate — the nine `false !== true` lines above.

Not run:
- `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` (full layers) were not run locally on this branch; CI runs them on this pull request.
- No browser/API/CLI journey was added: the change is a predicate inside the `web_fetch` URL guard, and the mocked E2E subset does not exercise NAT64/6to4 literals.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: a model-supplied `web_fetch` URL that encodes a private, loopback or link-local IPv4 address in NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated, Teredo or site-local form is now rejected with `PublicUrlError` instead of being fetched; public addresses in the same forms keep working.

Compatibility and migration: none. Public NAT64/6to4 egress is explicitly covered by the reverse assertions above.
922.head: dev2/fix/665-ipv6-embedded-ipv4
922.title: fix(web): judge NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local fetch targets by their embedded IPv4

924.author: HugoXK
924.body:
Fixes #839

A delimited dataset preview told the reader the file had as many columns as its widest line. A two-column `.csv` with one 5,000-field row was announced as `The file has 5000 columns; the preview shows the first 1001.` — a statement about a schema the file does not have. The column count now comes from the header; the wide row is reported as the cells it loses (`clippedCells`), not as columns.

## What was wrong

`parseDelimitedTable` derived one number, `totalColumns = Math.max(header.length, widest)`, and used it for two different jobs:

- the grid width (`width = min(totalColumns, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)`), which is a presentation cap, and
- `clippedColumns.total`, which the payload documents as *the file's own column count* and which the viewer prints verbatim when it exceeds `shown`.

For the issue's fixture — `a,b` header, 100 two-cell rows, one 5,000-field line as line 101, i.e. outside the default row window — the wide line is not a returned row at all. It still set `totalColumns = 5000`, so the payload reported `clippedColumns {shown: 1001, total: 5000}` and warned about 5,000 columns, while `clippedCells` was `0`: no returned cell was lost.

## What changed

`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`, `parseDelimitedTable` only:

- `totalColumns` is now `header.length` — the header is the schema; a data line is a row, not a column definition.
- `width` keeps its previous value, `min(max(header.length, widest), MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)`, so the rectangular payload, `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS`, `MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS` and the grid width are untouched. The width question in the issue title (a two-column file still renders 1,001 mostly-blank columns) is deliberately left to its own change; this one fixes the false number and the sentence built from it.
- The column warning still fires only when `total > shown`, which now means the header itself is wider than the preview — the case where "the file has N columns, the preview shows the first M" is true.

The payload contract is unchanged: `clippedColumns` keeps `{total, shown}` and `shown` keeps its width meaning; `clippedColumns.total` is the only value that changes, and `clippedCells` / `clippedColumns` are still reported separately.

Two existing assertions encoded the old meaning and are updated with it:

- `a delimited preview caps a pathological line and counts what it leaves out` — the wide line is inside the window there, so the payload now reports `{shown: 1001, total: 2}` and exactly one sentence, `199000 cells past the preview width are not shown.`
- `a long file does not cost a legitimate table its columns` — its fixture had a one-name header (`title`) over six-cell rows, so the header and the rows disagreed; the header now names all six columns (`title,a,b,c,d,e`) and the assertion `{shown: 6, total: 6}` still holds. The test's intent (file length must not cost a column) is unchanged.

## Red first

New test `a wide line past the row window does not become the file's column count`, run against the unfixed `parseDelimitedTable`:

```
not ok 63 - a wide line past the row window does not become the file's column count
  ---
  error: |-
    the file has as many columns as its header

    5000 !== 2

  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
  name: 'AssertionError'
  expected: 2
  actual: 5000
  operator: 'strictEqual'
# tests 67
# pass 66
# fail 1
```

## After the fix

```
# tests 67
# pass 67
# fail 0
```

The new test pins, for the fixture above: `clippedColumns.total === 2`; no warning matching `/has \d+ columns/`; `clippedCells === 0`; every returned row is as wide as the grid; and `columns.length` is *not* pinned, so the fix is provably scoped to the reported number, not to the grid width.

Diffstat against `main` `f4dd1813`:

```
 services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts | 17 ++++++++----
 services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts     | 50 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++---
 2 files changed, 57 insertions(+), 10 deletions(-)
```

Ran:
- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts` — `# tests 67 # pass 67 # fail 0`; the same file on the unfixed source is the red above (`# pass 66 # fail 1`).
- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.

Not run:
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` (the whole api suite) and the `ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e` layers were not run locally on this branch; CI runs them on this pull request.
- No browser journey: the rendered `DatasetTable` meta line is covered by the payload assertions here; the visual 1,001-column grid is the open width half of the issue, not this change.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: a delimited preview of a file with a wide data line no longer claims a column count the header does not have, and no longer warns about columns in the same breath as cells; a header genuinely wider than the preview still gets the column sentence.

Compatibility and migration: none. `clippedColumns` keeps its shape; only `total` changes for files whose widest line is wider than their header.
